subject: Data Engineering
title: Caching in Warehouses
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Caching in Warehouses.

hook.text: Run a query. It takes 10 seconds. Run the same query again. It returns in 100 milliseconds.

buildup.text: Warehouses cache query results so identical subsequent queries skip all computation.

discovery.text: Result caching, metadata caching, and local SSD caching are all layers that speed up repeated work.

twist.text: Cache invalidation happens when underlying data changes. Stale caches serve wrong answers.

climax.text: Understanding your warehouse's caching behavior explains why the same query has wildly different speeds.

punchline.text: The fastest query is the one already answered.

quiz.question: Why might the same query return faster on a second run?
options: The warehouse cached the result from the first run
